_rom_meta._this_key_is_new: Added 2026-08-03 together with the per-segment 'rom' key. Every field that existed before is untouched. Iterate segments by skipping keys that start with '_'.
_rom_meta.purpose: Multi-DOF range-of-motion limits, so the viewer can no longer rotate ball joints (shoulder/hip) a full 360 degrees.
_rom_meta.data_source: public/rom_data.json (AAOS standard normal ROM, reduced for this rig's static scapula / static pelvis; see that file for per-value confidence and citations).
_rom_meta.sign_convention: FLEXION-POSITIVE. flexion+/extension-, abduction+/adduction-, external rotation+/internal rotation-, supination+/pronation-, plantarflexion+/dorsiflexion-, inversion+/eversion-.
_rom_meta.relation_to_legacy_rom_deg: The pre-existing per-segment 'rom_deg' field uses the OPPOSITE sign for elbow and knee (flexion negative). It is deliberately left byte-identical. The application reads ONLY the new 'rom' key. Never wire both: rom_data.json warns that negating the angle AND flipping the axis cancels out.

rig_axis_binding._verified: Signs below were verified empirically in Babylon against public/fullbody_lite.glb on 2026-08-03, not derived on paper.
rig_axis_binding.frame: Per segment: down = rig rest direction (bone long axis); lateral = the abduction direction (-X for .l, +X for .r); front = +Z (anterior).
rig_axis_binding.flexion: rotates 'down' toward 'front' (knee is the exception: toward the back, flex_front_sign -1).
rig_axis_binding.abduction: rotates 'down' toward 'lateral'; positive is abduction on BOTH sides, so the left-side numbers below apply unmirrored.
rig_axis_binding.axial_rotation: about the bone long axis; positive is external rotation / supination on BOTH sides.
rig_axis_binding.composition_order: twist -> abduction -> flexion -> horizontal_adduction (extrinsic, parent space). Twist first so it is carried by the swing.

_rom_meta.ball_joint_note: Ball joints are clamped as a 2-DOF swing cone (abduction x flexion decomposed in the frame above) plus an independent twist, NOT as three unordered Euler clamps. This is the decomposition order that rom_data.json._meta.ball_joint_clamping_warning requires the wiring step to choose and document.
couplings_implemented: hip flexion max interpolates 80 (knee extended) -> 120 (knee flexed >= 90) [rom_data hip.dof.conditional]
ankle dorsiflexion max interpolates -20 (knee extended) -> -25 (knee flexed >= 90) [rom_data ankle.dof.conditional]
knee tibial rotation scales 0 at full extension -> full range at 90 deg knee flexion [rom_data knee.dof.available_only_when]

shoulder.l.note: multi-axis joint; no single hinge axis

rom.sign_convention: flexion-positive; see _rom_meta.sign_convention. Differs in sign from the legacy 'rom_deg' field in this same object, which is retained unchanged.
rom.values_stated_for: left side; the app mirrors the AXIS, not the numbers, so these apply unchanged to .r

dof.note: REDUCED FOR MODEL. AAOS shoulder-complex flexion is 180; scapulohumeral rhythm assigns ~2/3 of that to the glenohumeral joint, so pure GH flexion is ~120. Extension reduced from AAOS 60 to 50 for the same reason (scapular anterior tilt / downward rotation is unavailable).
dof.source: max (+120 flexion): AAOS 180 reduced via Inman, Saunders & Abbott 1944 scapulohumeral rhythm 2:1; 120 is the standard textbook glenohumeral share. min (-50 extension): ESTIMATE. AAOS gives 60 for the complex, but I found no source stating the glenohumeral-only share of extension, so 50 is my proportional guess. Tune freely.

dof.note: REDUCED FOR MODEL, TWICE OVER. (a) Elevation: AAOS complex abduction 180, of which ~60 is scapulothoracic upward rotation. Scapula is static here, so GH-only abduction caps at ~120. (b) Adduction: pure frontal-plane adduction from anatomical position is blocked by the trunk itself; the commonly quoted 30-50 requires slight flexion to bring the arm in front of the body. With a rigid humerus and no collision, allowing more will clip the ribcage mesh. Capped at 30.
dof.source: max (+120 abduction): AAOS 180 reduced via Inman, Saunders & Abbott 1944 (2:1 GH:ST ratio, ~120 GH + ~60 ST = 180). min (-30 adduction): ESTIMATE driven by mesh interpenetration with the ribcage, NOT by any source.

dof.note: AAOS values kept unreduced: axial rotation is predominantly glenohumeral, so the static scapula costs little here. Caveat: AAOS measures these at 90 degrees of abduction. With the arm at the side, internal rotation is blocked by the trunk at roughly 45 degrees in this collision-free model.
dof.source: AAOS: external rotation 90, internal rotation 70. The 45-degree arm-at-side internal rotation caveat is an ESTIMATE.

dof.note: Transverse-plane sweep measured at 90 deg abduction; positive sweeps the arm toward the midline. Not an AAOS DOF -- it is carried because pose_data.json drives bench press and flye with it.
dof.source: public/pose_data.json _meta.rom_used['shoulder.horizontal_adduction']

coupling_constraints.name: scapulohumeral_rhythm
coupling_constraints.description: Above roughly 30 degrees of elevation (the 'setting phase'), further humeral elevation requires scapular upward rotation in an approximately 2:1 glenohumeral:scapulothoracic ratio. 180 degrees of arm elevation = ~120 GH + ~60 ST.
coupling_constraints.why_it_matters_here: The scapula is in the static torso segment. So the model can only ever produce the GH half. Leaving the limit at 180 lets the humerus rotate to a position the real glenohumeral joint cannot reach, which reads as the arm tearing out of the shoulder socket -- this is the reported '360 degree rotation looks very weird' bug in its milder form.
coupling_constraints.action_taken: Both flexion and abduction capped at 120 rather than 180.
coupling_constraints.if_scapula_is_animated_later: Raise both to 180 and drive the scapula at half the humeral elevation angle.

coupling_constraints.name: trunk_collision
coupling_constraints.description: Adduction and arm-at-side internal rotation are limited in vivo by the trunk, not by the joint capsule.
coupling_constraints.why_it_matters_here: No collision detection and a rigid humerus mesh -- the arm will pass through the ribcage.
coupling_constraints.action_taken: Adduction capped at 30; a 45-degree arm-at-side internal rotation cap is recommended but left to the app.

dof.note: AAOS elbow flexion 150. joint_axes.json has 145 with the OPPOSITE sign -- see _meta.conflict_with_joint_axes_json. 0 to -10 of hyperextension is a common normal variant, more frequent in women.
dof.source: AAOS: elbow flexion 150, extension 0.

rom.sign_convention: flexion-positive; see _rom_meta.sign_convention. Differs in sign from the legacy 'rom_deg' field in this same object, which is retained unchanged.
rom.values_stated_for: left side; the app mirrors the AXIS, not the numbers, so these apply unchanged to .r

dof.note: TWO couplings. (1) AAOS hip flexion 120 is measured WITH THE KNEE FLEXED; with the knee extended, hamstring tension limits it to ~80-90. The knee is a separate rig segment so the app can implement this. (2) AAOS extension 30 includes lumbar lordosis compensation; the pelvis is the static rig root, so pure hip extension is REDUCED to 20.
dof.source: max (+120 flexion, knee flexed): AAOS hip flexion 120. min (-20 extension): ESTIMATE. AAOS gives 30, which includes lumbar lordosis compensation; I reduced it to 20 for the static-pelvis model limitation and found no source for a pure-hip extension figure.

conditional.source: 80 degrees is the standard clinical threshold for a normal passive straight-leg raise (below 80 is scored as hamstring tightness). Note this is the LOWER BOUND OF NORMAL rather than a population mean; sources quote 80-90 for knee-extended hip flexion. Verified this session; NOT attributed to any specific textbook.
conditional.note: Interpolate between this and max=120 as a function of knee flexion angle.

dof.note: AAOS values, unreduced. Caveat: adduction will interpenetrate the contralateral thigh mesh; ~20 is suggested if that looks wrong.
dof.source: AAOS: hip abduction 45, adduction 30. The 20-degree collision suggestion is an ESTIMATE.

dof.note: AAOS values. Measured in 90 degrees of hip flexion; in hip extension the capsule and ligaments are taut and available rotation is smaller (~30-35).
dof.source: AAOS: hip internal rotation 45, external rotation 45. The extended-hip 30-35 reduction is an ESTIMATE.

coupling_constraints.name: hamstring_two_joint_coupling
coupling_constraints.description: The hamstrings cross both hip and knee. Hip flexion of 120 requires knee flexion; with the knee straight the limit drops to ~80-90.
coupling_constraints.action_taken: max 120 recorded, with conditional.knee_extended_max_flexion = 90. The app should interpolate between them based on knee angle.

coupling_constraints.name: static_pelvis
coupling_constraints.description: Apparent hip extension in a live subject is substantially lumbar. The pelvis here is the static rig root.

knee.l.note: anatomical-position approximation (global medio-lateral); mesh-derived axes attempted and rejected as too noisy

rom.sign_convention: flexion-positive; see _rom_meta.sign_convention. Differs in sign from the legacy 'rom_deg' field in this same object, which is retained unchanged.
rom.values_stated_for: left side; the app mirrors the AXIS, not the numbers, so these apply unchanged to .r

dof.note: AAOS knee flexion 135. joint_axes.json has 140 with the OPPOSITE sign -- see _meta.conflict_with_joint_axes_json. Passive heel-to-buttock flexion reaches 150-160 but is not the standard active figure. 0 to -5 of hyperextension is a common normal variant.
dof.source: AAOS: knee flexion 135, extension 0.

dof.note: CONDITIONAL DOF. Axial tibial rotation is only available in flexion -- at full extension the screw-home mechanism locks it to near zero; maximum is around 90 degrees of knee flexion. Safe to omit entirely if the knee is driven as a pure hinge.
dof.source: NO SINGLE AUTHORITATIVE VALUE FOUND. Reported ranges vary widely between sources (roughly 10 internal / 20-30 external at 90 degrees of flexion). Standard biomechanics texts (Kapandji; Norkin & White) describe the motion and the screw-home mechanism, but I did not verify a specific figure. TREAT AS AN ESTIMATE.
dof.available_only_when: knee flexion > 20 degrees; scale linearly from 0 at full extension to full range at 90 degrees of flexion

ankle.l.note: anatomical-position approximation (global medio-lateral); mesh-derived axes attempted and rejected as too noisy; ankle axis is genuinely oblique -- treat as coarse

rom.sign_convention: flexion-positive; see _rom_meta.sign_convention. Differs in sign from the legacy 'rom_deg' field in this same object, which is retained unchanged.
rom.values_stated_for: left side; the app mirrors the AXIS, not the numbers, so these apply unchanged to .r

dof.note: AAOS values. These MATCH joint_axes.json exactly, including the sign -- no reconciliation needed for this joint. The 20 of dorsiflexion is measured with the knee extended; with the knee flexed the gastrocnemius slackens and a further 5-10 is available. The true talocrural axis is oblique, which joint_axes.json already flags as a coarse approximation.
dof.source: AAOS: ankle dorsiflexion 20, plantarflexion 50.

conditional.note: The gastrocnemius crosses both knee and ankle, so flexing the knee slackens it and releases roughly another 5-10 degrees of dorsiflexion. -25 is a deliberately round approximation; do not read precision into it.

rom.not_driveable_reason: joint_axes.json marks this segment type 'unmodelled' with axis null and rom_data.json flags it _not_currently_driveable: the segment holds only the calcaneus with no midfoot or forefoot distal to it. The app locks it at 0 rather than inventing an axis.
rom.sign_convention: flexion-positive; see _rom_meta.sign_convention. Differs in sign from the legacy 'rom_deg' field in this same object, which is retained unchanged.
rom.values_stated_for: left side; the app mirrors the AXIS, not the numbers, so these apply unchanged to .r

dof.note: SUBTALAR-PROPER value, not whole-foot. Literature converges on roughly 2/3 inversion and 1/3 eversion of a ~30-degree total arc, i.e. ~20 inversion and ~10 eversion from subtalar neutral. This will look almost invisible in the app because only the calcaneus moves -- that is the honest trade-off, do not inflate it for visibility.
dof.source: The 20/10 numbers come from the converging podiatric/biomechanics teaching figures I checked: subtalar total arc ~30 degrees, split roughly two-thirds inversion (~20) and one-third eversion (~10) from subtalar neutral. Inter-source spread is real (inversion reported 20-30, eversion 5-10), so treat 20/10 as the mid of a range, not a precise constant. Milgrom et al. 1985 is cited for establishing that subtalar-proper motion must be measured SEPARATELY from whole-foot motion -- these specific 20/10 numbers are NOT presented as that paper's measured result.

Not an anatomical joint: rig_config.json gives segment 'torso' pivot null, so the app derives a thoracolumbar pivot at runtime from the AABB of the 'Intervertebral disc T12-L1' mesh (L1-L5 and the sacrum belong to the pelvis segment, so T12-L1 is the actual seam). rig_config.json is NOT modified.

dof.note: LUMPED PROXY, not spinal ROM. For bent-over lifts the real motion is a hip hinge, but the rig is rooted at the pelvis, so hip flexion would swing the legs up instead of pitching the trunk down. 70 deliberately exceeds true thoracolumbar flexion.
dof.source: public/pose_data.json _meta.rom_used['torso.flexion'] and _meta.torso_caveat
